name: Pasir Ris
summary: Quiet east-coast-adjacent HDB town with EWL access, Pasir Ris Park, and Downtown East — family-leaning and calmer than Tampines or Bedok hubs.
body: Pasir Ris is the chill east shortlist when Tampines feels too packed and Bedok still too hub-loud. Pasir Ris MRT on the East-West Line, White Sands / town-centre errands, and Pasir Ris Park / Downtown East weekends define the lifestyle; airport-side hops are a quiet plus for frequent travellers. Housing is mostly HDB with selective condo and executive stock — rents usually undercut Katong and many Tampines projects for similar bedroom counts because you trade some night-life density for space and park access. Commute west or to CBD is the honest cost: EWL length is real even when car rides feel shorter than reputation. Watch-outs: some blocks sit a long walk from the MRT despite the town label, weekend park crowds, and flash-flood / low-approach checks near park edges on storm days. Compare with Tampines for denser self-contained east living, Bedok for closer EWL + town-centre gravity, or Punggol if you want newer northeast flats instead of east-park vibes.
bestFor: car-optional households okay with longer CBD rides
watchOuts: Longer EWL CBD commute vs central towns
housingMix: HDB majority, selective condo and executive pockets, park-adjacent stacks.
commuteNotes: East-West Line at Pasir Ris; time door-to-desk and the actual feeder/walk from your block.
